newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BENFICA HUMBLED BY CRUZEIRO'S RESERVES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BENFICA HUMBLED BY CRUZEIRO'S RESERVES.

text.p: Benfica's newly-assembled, multi-million dollar team were humbled Sunday as they were beaten 4-1 by Brazilian club Cruzeiro, who fielded a reserve team.

Cruzeiro's top players were rested for the match in the Copa Centenario tournament as they are away to Peruvian champions Sporting Cristal in the first leg of the South American Libertadores Cup on Wednesday.
But the reserves did Cruzeiro proud as they came from behind to hammer the Portuguesa side, which is using the tournament as part of its pre-season warm-up.

Two spectacular goals from 17-year-old midfielder Geovani put Cruzeiro in command in the second half after Roberto Gaucho had wiped out Benfica's lead with a penalty just before halftime. Fabio Junior scored the fourth with a header.

Benfica, whose polyglot team contains players from Brazil, Paraguay, Bolivia, England and Morocco, went ahead in the group B match when new Brazilian signee Paulo Nunes slipped through the Cruzeiro defence and scored.

Earlier, Flamengo of Brazil had come from two goals behind to draw 2-2 with Paraguay's Olimpia, who stood in at the last minute when Argentina's San Lorenzo pulled out because of a player's strike in their country.
The tournament, which also features local clubs Atletico Mineiro and America, Italy's Milan and Corinthians from Sao Paulo, is being played to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the city's founding.
